headline: The first pipelines move to serverless

items.title: uniware-sync runs on ECS Fargate
items.detail: Our biggest pipeline left its server. It now runs as a scheduled container behind a fixed IP that Unicommerce allowlists.

items.title: meta-sync live on Fargate
items.detail: Meta Ads spend and insights for both ad accounts load daily, with no NAT cost.

items.title: Sajid's invoice pipeline deployed
items.detail: Sajid Ali's Unicommerce invoice sync now runs inside our dbt staging and reporting layers, rebuilt every day.

items.title: B2B dashboards by Sajid
items.detail: Sajid built 4 B2B dashboards on top of it in Metabase: stuck invoices, master inventory, fill rate and daily run rate.

items.title: Landing zone for raw API data
items.detail: Every raw Unicommerce response is kept in S3 and moves to cheaper storage tiers after 30 and 180 days.

items.title: Courier scoring v2 and v3
items.detail: Shadowfax and marketplace couriers added, with a courier-level prior for scoring.

items.title: Data quality checks
items.detail: Fixed the Flipkart test and added a check for partial Unicommerce loads.

items.title: One owner per table
items.detail: Cleanup finished: every table has a single owner and scheduling moved to dbt.

items.title: Courier selection deck: 4 questions
items.detail: COD vs prepaid RTO (COD's RTO is about 7x prepaid's), each courier's COD mix, the scoring weight scenarios and a pincode lookup that names the best courier for COD and for prepaid orders.

explain.simple: Explains why couriers are now ranked separately for COD and prepaid orders, and lets ops pick a courier for any pincode.
explain.technical: Last 90 days, closed shipments, Shopify; couriers with 500+ shipments; pincode lookup reads reporting.courier_scoring (0.10 cost + 0.30 NDR + 0.50 RTO + 0.10 speed); weight scenarios are the static output of the 2026-10-12 simulation.

items.title: Customer support orders with the previous order
items.detail: Every order the support team created, next to the same customer's previous order, with a flag for which ones are replacements.

explain.simple: Lets us see what each support-created order was for.
explain.technical: staging.orders, Shopify, 'Customer support' tag; previous order of the same customer; is_replacement = discount reason mentions 'previous'.

items.title: Shopify SKU run-rate and projection
items.detail: SKU-wise daily sales run-rate over a chosen window, projected to a full month, at inventory SKU level (combos split into their parts).

explain.simple: How many units of each product we will sell this month at the current pace.
explain.technical: Component SKU = product_master.internal_code; units / days in window x projection days; start_date, end_date, projection_days variables.

items.title: Retention cohort by category
items.detail: Monthly retention cohorts in customer counts and %, overall and per category, last 13 months, in the same layout as the September retention sheet.

explain.simple: Of the customers who first bought in a month, how many came back in each later month, per category.
explain.technical: Shopify; cohort = first-order month; m0..m12 counts and % versions kept in step; choco = 3 Shopify product ids.

items.title: Net Sales trend by category, New vs Repeat
items.detail: Net Sales by day, week or month for each category, split new and repeat customers, ready for a line or stacked bar.

explain.simple: Shows whether each category's sales come from new or returning customers over time.
explain.technical: reporting.shopify_pnl_daily_by_category_customer_type; long format, series = category - New/Repeat; card 142.

items.title: Category month on month, New vs Repeat
items.detail: Last 12 complete months per category with a Total row, New and Repeat separately.

explain.simple: A monthly view of each category for new and returning customers.
explain.technical: reporting.shopify_pnl_daily_by_category_customer_type; one row per month x customer type x category + Total; optional customer_type filter.
